(1) FLAGSHIP 0x17: a subgroup battery (simd_ballot/simd_any/simd_all/simd_active_threads_mask/simd_is_first/simd_sum/simd_min/simd_max/simd_prefix_exclusive_sum/simd_broadcast[_first]/simd_shuffle[_up/down/xor]) compiled and tokenized -> the ONLY real byte0-0x17 ops emitted are simd_ballot (byte+1 low-nib 7: 0x07 active/any/all, 0x17 ballot(pred)), ALL already NAMED (sg.hex: 0x17 named=3, lenonly=6). All 6 length_only 0x17 in the same own shader are `17 05`/`17 02` iadd2 tails preceded by a mis-lengthed n3_mov/fspecial/float-ALU (proven by context dump: e.g. `... 03 20 18 a8 | 17 05 47 04 54 ..` where `a8 17 05` is the iadd tail and `47 04 54 ..` is the next simd_shuffle). (2) THIRDPARTY 17.05 (191/278 = 69% of tp length_only) identically shown to be cascade: `falu3_srcmod12 59 0f 3a 15 9f 01 54 04 02 24 10 a8 | 17 05 39 0b ..` -- the 0x59 float-ALU extended-source length `6+2*(b4&3)` returns 12 because byte+4 == 0x9f (the FOLLOWING iadd's opcode), over-reading 6 bytes of a real `9f 01 54 .. a8 17 05` iadd2 and exposing its `17 05` tail. (3) OWN 0x47.8x family (`47 XX 02 82 05 02 80 ZZ 27 00`, byte+1 marching by 2): context dump shows each preceded by a `32 88` isel desync -- cascade from byte0-0x32 isel mis-length, NOT a real 0x47 shuffle (real shuffle requires byte+2 in {0x54,0x56}; these have byte+2==0x02). (4) desync roots 07.02/54.0d/02.02/02.08/82.10 traced to upstream culprits (isel tails `07 02`/`17 02`, half-ALU 0x10, mov/tg 0x1c, float-ALU). enum_desync.py safety test: the top desync sigs are safe=False (their byte0 is a real op-leader elsewhere), so a blanket 2-byte close is UNSAFE. The safe=True sigs are single-parcel trailing words whose 2-byte close only RELABELS desync->length_only (net-zero on the combined length_only+desync metric) -> not pursued. (5) 27.02 candidate: provoked extract_bits/insert_bits with constant AND runtime-variable offset/count -> our own MSL emits only NAMED ibfins/ibfe/ibitcount, never the byte+1==0x02 form; it sits at clean boundaries in conversions_pack/cvt_i64 so it is a REAL ibfins-family variant we cannot provoke -> unresolved (no fabricated fields).

censusBothCorpora.note: 0x17 (both) + 0x47 (own) account for ~68-69% of ALL length_only tokens on each corpus. BOTH proven cascade below. Residual is thus ~entirely upstream-cascade; there is no undecoded-new-opcode residue to name.

whyNoChange: Every safe, honest lever was evaluated and rejected: (a) authoring 0x17/0x47 descriptors would type cascade/operand bytes as instructions -> FORBIDDEN (fabrication / metric-gaming). (b) R9-style guarded 2-byte closes of the residual desync sigs either target safe=False sigs (would swallow real ops -> regress) or safe=True single-parcel words whose close merely RELABELS a desync region into a length_only token (net-zero on the combined length_only+desync goal; strictly increases the length_only half). (c) The genuine fix -- correcting the over-reading upstream length rules (float-ALU 0x09/0x59 extended-source `6+2*(b4&3)` when byte+4 is a following op's opcode; half-ALU 0x10; isel 0x02/0x12/0x22/0x32/0x42 tail bracketing; fspecial 0x2f; mov/tg 0x1c) -- would move bytes from BOTH length_only and desync into NAMED, but it touches the highest-frequency ops in the ISA and cannot be proven zero-regression without dedicated own-MSL length experiments per family (out of a residual-close scope, and the wrong fix regresses hundreds of files). (d) deleting the 423 operand_word_* descriptors without predecessor-length absorption would turn NAMED operand tokens into length_only/desync -> regress. All four are correctly owned by the length-rule maintainer; see unresolved[].
